sources.title: Hangzhou Longjing Tea Plantations: Learn Chinese Tea Culture
sources.content:
Complete Text Content: Longjing Tea Plantations in Hangzhou

Overview & Introduction
Hangzhou is celebrated as a cultural hub of eastern China that has preserved local traditions. The city serves as the origin of the world-famous Longjing tea. The Longjing Tea Plantations in the southwestern region of West Lake represent a production site covering 240 hectares, spanning eight villages including Longjing, Manjuelong, and Jiuxi.

Fast Facts
Location: Southwest of West Lake, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China
Opening time: All day
Ticket price: Villages are free to enter but certain attractions may require a fee
Recommended visit time: 2-5 hours
Best time to visit: March and April for tea-picking
Suited to: Anyone interested in Chinese tea culture and natural scenery

About Longjing Tea
Longjing (Dragon Well Tea) is a pan-roasted green tea cultivated in Hangzhou, recognized for its vibrant green color, refreshing fragrance, and mild taste. Rich in health benefits, it carries over 1,200 years of history.

Historical Account: Emperor Qianlong visited Shifeng Village when learning his mother was ill. Upon returning to Beijing with Longjing tea, his mother improved after smelling and tasting it. The emperor subsequently ordered the finest Longjing tea annually.

Harvesting & Preparation: Tea collection occurs before or around Qingming Festival in early April. Leaves are hand-fried in woks to remove moisture. For home preparation, steep tea in 80 degrees C water for 3 minutes.

Top Longjing Tea Plantations

Meijiawu Tea Village: Located in the western region of West Lake, Meijiawu features a history exceeding 600 years. Activities include tea-picking with local farmers, observing hand-frying of leaves, attending traditional tea ceremonies, and purchasing tea directly from villagers.

Longjing Village: Located in southwestern area of West Lake, designated the "No. 1 Village of Tea" as the birthplace of Longjing tea. Generations of farmers have built fields against green hills.

Shifeng Mountain: Located south of West Lake, ranks among Hangzhou's oldest and most esteemed plantations. Fewer crowds than Meijiawu and Longjing Village.

Wengjiashan: Positioned on the southwest side of West Lake, center of West Lake Longjing tea production area. Tea planting history traces back to the Ming Dynasty. Encompasses 1,040 acres of Longjing tea, with green areas accounting for 81.3% of total area.

Manjuelong Village: Located at the southern foot of Nanfeng Peak. "Manjuelong Osmanthus Rain" ranks among the new West Lake's ten scenic spots.

Geographic Classification
Only tea produced in the West Lake District can be called "West Lake Longjing"; other areas produce "Longjing tea" instead.

First-level area (five core production areas): Shisheng, Longjing, Yunqi, Hupao, and Meijiaowu
Second-level area: All West Lake District Longjing tea excluding first-level sources

Transportation
The plantations are approximately 15 km (9 miles) from downtown Hangzhou. Taxi about 30 minutes. Public Bus Routes 27, 87, or Y3 travel directly to Longjing Village or Meijiawu Village.

UNESCO Recognition
In 2022, "Traditional Chinese Tea-making Techniques and Their Associated Customs" was included in UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.

sources.title: Hangzhou Attractions | Dragon Well Tea Village
sources.content:
Dragon Well Tea Plantation in Hangzhou: Complete Information

Overview
Longjing tea, or "Dragon Well tea," is one of China's most famous green teas, celebrated for its delicate flavor and rich aroma. The tea originates from hills surrounding Hangzhou and features jade-green leaves with a flat appearance.

Historical Development
Before the Sui and Tang Dynasties, tea culture was in early stages. During the Northern Song Dynasty, the Longjing tea-growing region formed on a preliminary scale, with Xianglin, Baiyun, and Baoyun teas becoming tribute offerings. Emperor Qianlong visited four times, wrote six imperial poems, and personally sealed "the eighteen royal tea trees."

Dragon Well Tea Village (Longjing Village)
Location: Southwest of West Lake scenic area
Population: approximately 800 people
Tea garden area: nearly 800 acres of high mountain terrain
Natural barriers: Beigao Peak, Lion Peak, Tianzhu Peak (northwest)

Meijiawu Tea Village
Located 13 km west of West Lake, approximately 30 minutes' drive. Described as "the most real and original place where produces Dragon Well tea in Hangzhou." The village has been visited by Queen Elizabeth and Bill Clinton.
Getting There: By bus No. 28 from Tiyuchang Lu stop, transfer to No. 27 at Yu Quan stop. By taxi: RMB 35-45.
Hours: Open all day. Admission: Free. Best season: March to May.

Activities & Experiences
Tea Picking: Participate in traditional leaf-plucking from bushes.
Tea Tasting & Brewing: Guided sessions sampling different Longjing grades.
Traditional Tea Ceremonies: Learn cultural significance.
Stir-Frying Experience (Chao Cha): Learn traditional pan-frying methods.

Seasonal Visit Guide
Spring (March-May) - Peak Season: Best for tea picking during first flush harvest. "Mingqian" tea (pre-Qingming leaves) is most prized.
Summer (June-August): Ideal for scenic views without crowds.
Autumn (September-November): Great for photography and fall foliage.
Winter (December-February): Focus on tea museums and workshops.

Tea Varieties by Harvest Time
Mingqian Longjing (Pre-Qingming): Harvested late March to early April. Highest quality.
Yuqian Longjing (Post-Qingming): Mid-April before Grain Rain.
Guyu Longjing (Grain Rain): Late April to early May.

How to Brew Longjing Tea
Use filtered or spring water at 80–85°C. Use 3-5 grams per 180 ml cup. Steep 1–2 minutes for first infusion. Allows 3-4 infusions.

sources.title: Hangzhou Tea Plantation, Visit Longjing Tea Plantation
sources.content:
Hangzhou Tea Plantation, Visit Longjing Tea Plantation

Longjing Tea, also known as Dragon Well Tea, has a history of over 1200 years and is acclaimed as the premier tea in China, often referred to as the "Green Queen." Meijiawu Village and Longjing Village are two excellent choices for visiting Longjing Tea plantations in Hangzhou.

The tea-picking season in Hangzhou usually spans from late March to early November, during which tourists can participate in the tea-picking process and relish the newly harvested Longjing Tea. Early spring, March and April, is the best time.

The five main production regions are Lion Peak (Shi Feng) Mountain, Longjing Village, Five Cloud (Wuyun) Mountain, Tiger Running (Hupao) Temple and Meijiawu. Meijiawu Village teems with Longjing Tea and is very famous for the five visits of the great Prime Minister Zhou Enlai.

For the best experience and views, visit early in the morning. You can take a bamboo basket and pick tea with local tea pickers. After that, return with them to their homes and watch how they hand-fry the leaves. They'll treat you to a tea tasting showing you the traditional tea ceremony.

From central Hangzhou, take buses #27, #87 or #180. The most convenient way is to take a taxi—the journey takes about 40-60 minutes.

sources.title: How I Explored Longjing Tea Village in Hangzhou, China
sources.content:
How I Explored Longjing Tea Village in Hangzhou, China

The article describes a detailed travel guide to Longjing (龙井), both a village and tea production area located in hills west of West Lake in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province.

Scholars have been attracted to Longjing area for over a thousand years. Tea production began during the Southern Song dynasty (12th-13th centuries). In the Qing dynasty, Emperor Qianlong visited and was so impressed with tea from 18 specific bushes that he granted them imperial status as "The Royal 18 Trees."

Longjing sits approximately 150 kilometers from Shanghai. West Lake, the famous UNESCO World Heritage site, is nearby.

The article covers: Best timing for visits, transportation methods to reach the village, specific locations including Green Tea Restaurant, China National Tea Museum, and Longjing Temple, walking routes through tea fields, tea tasting experiences, purchasing guidelines and pricing information, and the historic 18 Royal Trees location.

English-language resources about practical visitor information were scarce, motivating the author to create this comprehensive guide. Take local bus 27 (¥2, 25 minutes, frequent) from anywhere along the northern shore of West Lake and get off at the Longjing Tea Village stop.

sources.title: 龙井茶园_百度百科
sources.content:
龙井茶园完整内容

基本信息
龙井茶园位于中国浙江省杭州市西湖景区周边，是传统茶园，核心产区涵盖狮峰、龙井、云栖等地，以出产西湖龙井茶闻名。

地理位置与自然条件
茶园地处丘陵地带，土壤肥沃且常年云雾环绕。位于北纬30度附近，三面环山、一面临江伴湖。钱塘江风与西湖水汽交汇形成温润的云雾气候。狮子峰、龙井、灵隐、五云山、虎跑、梅家坞一带土地肥沃，多为含有机物磷较高的微酸性沙质土壤。

历史发展
其历史可追溯至唐代寺院茶文化。北宋辩才法师种植龙井茶树开创禅茶文化。宋代因文士推崇逐渐兴盛。1949年前按产地分为"狮、龙、云、虎、梅"五类，后合并为"狮、龙、梅"三系。龙井茶自宋代得名，清代乾隆帝御封"十八棵御茶"后声名远播，现为中国十大名茶之一。

传说典故
清朝乾隆皇帝下江南时品尝龙井新茶，看到采茶姑娘技艺精湛也学着采摘。接到太后生病消息后将采到的茶叶放在袖子里匆匆赶回北京。太后饮后病体痊愈，乾隆特意把西湖龙井寺前的十八棵茶树册封为"御茶"。因茶叶在袖中被压成扁平状，后来的西湖龙井也被制作成这种特殊形状。2005年拍卖会上，所谓"御茶"每100克成交价为14.56万元。

产地分类
西湖龙井茶按产地分为"狮、龙、云、虎、梅"五个品类。现代分类为"狮、龙、梅"三品类。产于西湖乡龙井村的称为"狮字龙井"，自然品质最好。产于梅家坞、梵村、云栖一带的称为"梅字龙井"，做工精湛。

核心产区
西湖龙井茶一级保护基地5000多亩分布在西湖景区范围内。重点产茶村是翁家山、龙井、满觉陇、杨梅岭、梅家坞、双峰等村庄。

采茶方法
全年采摘期190天～200天，一棵茶树一年可采摘22次。采摘的茶叶应为长度不超过两厘米的鲜叶。谚语："早采三天是个宝，迟采三天变成草。"

茶叶等级
品质最高的是清明以前采摘的"明前茶"。清明以后、谷雨以前的"雨前茶"品质稍逊。精挑细选的嫩芽叫"莲心"；一芽一叶叫"旗枪"；一芽两叶叫"雀舌"。

传统制茶工艺
包含手工"青锅"和"辉锅"两道工序。青锅每锅放鲜叶约120克，锅温240℃～300℃，炒至七八成干约12～15分钟。辉锅约100℃，炒制20～25分钟。龙井茶传统炒制技艺于2008年被列为国家级非物质文化遗产。

炒茶特点
一个熟练的炒茶能手一天只能炒1000克左右干茶。品质上乘的西湖龙井都是手工炒制的。老一代炒茶工往往从十几岁开始学徒，历经二三十年磨练才能成熟。

冲泡方法
饮龙井茶最好用虎跑泉水。茶具以透明无花玻璃杯为最佳。茶叶与水比例约1∶50，先注入四分之一杯水浸润茶叶。"凤凰三点头"冲泡手法让茶叶充分接触水。龙井茶可冲泡三次，第二次味道最好。

现代发展
2025年首次使用无人机监测芽叶生长状态，并引入AI采茶机器人。2026年春分时节举行"龙井问茶"开茶仪式。西湖龙井茶与西湖一样，是人、自然、文化三者的重要结晶。

sources.title: 杭州龙井村游玩攻略
sources.content:
杭州龙井村游玩攻略

龙井村本身是免费开放的。老龙井御茶园（老龙井十八棵御茶园）的门票为10元。

春季是游玩龙井村的最佳季节，春天是西湖龙井春茶的采摘期。

老龙井御茶园里有九溪源、十八棵御茶、宋广福院、龙泓、胡公馆、胡公墓、辩才亭、辩才塔等景观景点。

交通：可以乘27路和游3路等公交到龙井村站下车。

龙井村内购买茶叶时，砍价是必须的，一般可砍到要价的一半或六成左右。此外，春季可以体验亲手采摘明前龙井，导游会讲解龙井茶的等级、炒制工艺，之后在茶农家品一杯现泡的龙井新茶。

sources.title: Longjing Tea Village | Hangzhou - Lonely Planet
sources.content:
Longjing Tea Village - Lonely Planet

Most places at Hangzhou Longjing tea plantations do not need tickets, and you can walk around the tea villages and hills for free, though some gardens or museums might ask for tickets. Meijiawu Tea Village has all-day opening hours with free entrance fee.

The China National Tea Museum has free entrance. The Upper Branch has a small entry fee of RMB 10.

Spring is the best time to visit, when straw-hatted workers can be seen picking the tea leaves by hand in the fields.

Take local bus 27 (¥2, 25 minutes, frequent) from anywhere along the northern shore of West Lake and get off at the Longjing Tea Village stop.

Visitors can wander through the village and up into the tea plantations, and stop into casual restaurants and teahouses to taste the longjing tea.
